page: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Epdsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache, with one thread per core. This instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 1890 GB local disk, and the server is premium storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance and top-tier memory capabilities. The E32pds_v6 achieves a strong multi-core CPU performance score of 66297.85 in stress-ng and a strong Geekbench multi-core score of 20088.0. Memory bandwidth is a key strength, with read-only large block bandwidth reaching a top-tier 449.0 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 188.31 GB/sec. Passmark memory testing ranks in the top tier with a score of 3327.28. Database operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by a top-tier Passmark database score of 37819.86 and a strong Redis SET performance of 61.82 million operations per second. Single-core performance is moderate, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core scores falling in the average category. Large-scale LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 70B model rated as poor at 4.65 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based architecture provides a high density of dedicated physical cores and substantial memory capacity without the premium associated with traditional x86 memory-optimized instances. The inclusion of a large 1890 GB local disk adds further value for data-intensive operations. This server is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, relational and non-relational database hosting, Redis caching layers, software compilation, and high-throughput static web serving.
